title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is rotated 90°, cancelled by long diagonal pencil strokes, and written mostly in Grothendieck's private abbreviations. Only the formulas can be read with any confidence. This reconstruction is therefore tentative.

What the formulas suggest:
- A category written 𝒞 (or 𝒟_S) whose objects are diagrams (S ← T_0 → T). Here T_0 → T is presumably a closed immersion: a nilpotent thickening, possibly with divided powers.
- A functor F defined on this category.
- Morphisms between such objects, written u : T → U, compatible with the maps to S: t_0 = f_0 (the second t_0 might be a misread u_0).
- A comparison of two objects (S ← U_0 → U) and (S ← T_0 → T), drawn as a square with dotted arrows U_0 ⋯ T_0 and U ⋯ T, with a point φ_0 marked above it. This looks like the extension/lifting condition one checks when building a crystal or an infinitesimal/crystalline site.
- The special object U = U_0 = S with t_0 = id. This is the trivial thickening of S, i.e. the base point at which the functor is to be evaluated.
- A side remark '(AS…)', perhaps meaning 'Artin-Schreier' or 'as above'; unclear.

Context:
- The previous page computes the obstruction class involving ω^{⊗p} − F*(Cω) (the Cartier operator) and a map from Pic to a vector-bundle-like quotient.
- The next page opens 'Connexion canonique de Gauss-Manin. Partie 2'.

The most plausible reading is a first, abandoned attempt to set up the formal framework for the canonical Gauss–Manin connection. That framework expresses the connection as crystal-type descent data: a functor F on the category 𝒟_S of S-thickenings (S ← T_0 → T), compared on the diagonal-type objects. This is the standard approach of Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES 1966, in Dix exposés, 1968) and of Katz–Oda. The strike-through indicates that Grothendieck discarded this draft and restarted in 'Partie 2'.
errors: Too little is legible to check correctness, and the page is crossed out (abandoned draft). No mathematical error can be identified.

ideas.what: A functor F on a category of thickenings (S ← T_0 → T) over a base S, used to define the Gauss–Manin connection via crystals / descent data on infinitesimal neighbourhoods.
ideas.modern_name: Crystals on the infinitesimal/crystalline site; crystalline description of the Gauss–Manin connection
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Evaluation at the trivial thickening U = U_0 = S with t_0 = id.
ideas.modern_name: Value of a crystal at the trivial object (S, S)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an illegible, crossed-out draft. As far as it can be read, it sets up standard crystal-type formalism for the Gauss–Manin connection, which Grothendieck had already published in 1966/68.
transcription_corrections: The whole page is cancelled by diagonal strokes; its content should be treated as a discarded draft.
The repeated symbol read as '𝒟_S' could be the name of the category of S-thickenings. The expression read as '𝒞_?(S ← T_0 → T)' is likely '𝒞 = (S ← T_0 → T)', i.e. a description of the objects of 𝒞.
The diagram is a square with dotted arrows U_0 ⋯ T_0 and U ⋯ T, with φ_0 written above the upper arrow; it is not two separate lines.
Last formula line: 'U = U_0 = S, t_0 = id' (i.e. j = id).
